coin-walk.title: Coin flip or chart pattern?
coin-walk.short: Prices made only of coin flips. Every trend and every pattern is noise.

lln-clt.title: Law of large numbers and the central limit theorem
lln-clt.short: The average of many draws approaches the expected value, and sample means pile up into a bell curve.
lln-clt.summary: {mode, select, lln {After {count} draws the average is {value}; the expected value is {mu}.} other {{count} sample means: average {value} (expected {mu}), spread {sd} (theory σ/√n = {se}).}}

gbm.title: Brownian motion and geometric Brownian motion
gbm.short: Hundreds of possible price paths over a year, and the distribution of their values at every moment.
gbm.summary: Step {step} of {steps}, {paths} paths: mean {mean}, median {median}, expected value {expected}.

monte-carlo.title: Monte Carlo method
monte-carlo.short: Estimating π and an option price by random sampling, with the error shrinking like 1/√N.
monte-carlo.summary: After {count} samples: estimate {estimate}, true value {truth}, error {error}, 95% margin ±{margin}.

martingale.title: Martingale: doubling the bet
martingale.short: A thousand players double their bet after every loss. Most win a little for a long time, while the share of ruined players rises every round.
martingale.summary: Round {round} of {rounds}: {ruined}% of players are ruined. Average bankroll {mean} (start {start}).

kelly.title: Kelly criterion
kelly.short: The same bets played with half, full and double the Kelly stake. Betting too much grows slower, and can even lose despite an edge.
kelly.summary: Bet {bet} of {bets}. Kelly stakes {kelly}% of capital. Typical wealth (geometric average): ½ Kelly {half}, Kelly {full}, 2× Kelly {double}. Theoretical growth per bet: {gHalf}%, {gFull}%, {gDouble}%.

vol-drag.title: Volatility drag
vol-drag.short: With the same average yearly return, the typical investor ends up far below the average. Volatility makes the difference.
vol-drag.summary: Year {year} of {years}: mean wealth {mean}, typical (median) {median}. The average return is {mu}% a year; compounded it is about {geo}%.

ev-heatmap.title: Expected value map
ev-heatmap.short: Win rate, reward to risk and costs together. Blue cells make money, orange ones lose it, and the line is break-even.
ev-heatmap.summary: Win rate {p}%, reward to risk {rr}, costs {fees} R: expected value {ev} R per trade. At this RR you need to win at least {breakEven}% of trades.

overfitting.title: Backtest overfitting
overfitting.short: Hundreds of strategies that are pure noise. The best one in sample looks brilliant; out of sample it is as random as the rest.
overfitting.summary: {mode, select, oos {The best of {strategies} random strategies had an in-sample Sharpe of {isSharpe}; out of sample it has {oosSharpe}. Median in sample of all: {median}.} other {Day {day}. The best of {strategies} random strategies has an in-sample Sharpe of {isSharpe}; the median of all is {median}. None has an edge.}}

fourier.title: Fourier: a signal and its spectrum
fourier.short: Build a signal from three sines and see three clear peaks in its spectrum. A random walk's spectrum has no peaks; it just falls.
fourier.summary: {source, select, walk {The random walk's spectrum falls as a power of frequency: slope {slope} (theory −2), with no clear peaks.} other {Strongest frequencies: {p1}, {p2} and {p3} cycles per window.}}

bayes.title: Bayes: a strategy's true win rate
bayes.short: After every trade the posterior for the win rate narrows. A few dozen trades say surprisingly little.
bayes.summary: After {trades} trades ({wins} wins): posterior mean {mean}%, 95% interval from {lo}% to {hi}%. Chance the win rate is above 50%: {edge}%. True value: {truth}%.

option-builder.title: Option builder
option-builder.short: Build a position from one or two options and see the payoff at expiry, the Black–Scholes value today and the Greeks.
option-builder.summary: The position costs {value} today. At a stock price of {S}: delta {delta}, gamma {gamma}, vega {vega} per volatility point, theta {theta} per day.
